title: AMD Beats on Revenue and EPS, Guides Q4 to $17 Billion; Shares Rise About 8% After Hours
dek: AMD reported fiscal third-quarter revenue of $13.38 billion and adjusted EPS of $2.09, both above estimates, and guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $17 billion. Apple ended the session down 1.90% on margin worries.
author: Meridian Newsroom

keyPoints: AMD reported adjusted EPS of $2.09 against $1.95 expected, and revenue of $13.38 billion against $13.09 billion expected (CNBC, LSEG).
Data center revenue hit a record $8.5 billion, up 97% from a year earlier (AMD).
AMD guided fourth-quarter revenue to about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%, against an LSEG average estimate of $16.2 billion (CNBC, AMD).
Shares rose about 8% in extended trading after falling three straight days (CNBC).
Apple ended down 1.90% in regular trading, about $94 billion below Monday's close, after a weaker margin forecast (Stock Titan).
body:
## AMD: beat, record data center, stronger guidance

Advanced Micro Devices reported fiscal third-quarter 2026 results after the close on Tuesday. Revenue rose 45% from a year earlier to $13.38 billion, against $13.09 billion expected by LSEG. Adjusted earnings were $2.09 a share, against $1.95 expected (CNBC, AMD).

Data center revenue was a record $8.5 billion, up 97% year over year, driven by EPYC processors and the launch of Instinct MI450 GPUs (AMD). Client and gaming revenue was $3.7 billion, down 8%, and gaming alone fell 40% (AMD, CNBC).

## Guidance: the number investors were waiting for

AMD expects fourth-quarter revenue of about $17 billion, plus or minus 3%. That is above the $16.2 billion LSEG average (CNBC). Benzinga put the expected adjusted gross margin at about 55%, against 56% in the third quarter (Benzinga).

On the earnings call, Chief Executive Lisa Su said she expects server revenue to double in 2027 and that AI data center growth will accelerate faster than the company projected three months ago (CNBC).

## Stock move

The shares rose about 8% in extended trading after three straight sessions of losses tied to fears of overspending on AI infrastructure (CNBC). The stock is up roughly 125% this year (CNBC). The after-hours move is an early read; regular-session trading on Wednesday will show whether the gain holds.

## Apple closed lower

Apple ended the regular session down 1.90%, about $94 billion below Monday's close, after warning that rising memory costs would squeeze margin per dollar of revenue (Stock Titan, AP). The move was the largest drag on the Dow.

## What to watch

Three items matter for Wednesday. First, whether AMD's after-hours gain holds once the regular session opens. Second, whether the fourth-quarter guidance eases concern about AI spending across the chip group. Third, whether Apple's margin warning spreads to other hardware makers.

marketImpact.summary: AMD beat on revenue and earnings and guided above consensus. Its data center growth and guidance are the main test for the chip rebound. Apple's margin warning is a separate, smaller signal for hardware.
marketImpact.timeframe: After-hours Tuesday, Nov. 3, through Wednesday's open
